summary: Source decomposition from four primary sources read directly: Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams Appendix B (printed pp. 79-81), Pollack-Stevens 'Critical slope p-adic L-functions' (Sections 1, 2, 3.1-3.2, 8 and 9), Bellaiche 'Critical p-adic L-functions' (Sections 1.1-1.4), and Amice-Velu (Theoreme III, printed p. 125). Formulas (2) of Pollack-Stevens and (4)-(5) of Bellaiche were read from rendered page images at 220 and 500 dpi because the PDF text layers scramble the fractions and drop a bar on Q-bar_p. TWO PRINTED DISCREPANCIES ARE RECORDED. (1) Pollack-Stevens equation (2) prints L(f, chi^{-1}, 1) as the interpolated value, but its left-hand side depends on j and no other factor supplies that dependence; Bellaiche, restating the same Pollack-Stevens interpolation property, prints L_infinity(f phi^{-1}, j+1), which fixes the reading. (2) Bellaiche's modification factor (5) prints alpha in BOTH Euler-factor denominators while its prefactor is 1/beta^nu and the refinement being interpolated is f_beta with U_p f_beta = beta f_beta; by Bellaiche's own Sec. 1.3 the denominators should be beta. The reconciliation of RJW Theorem B.1 (one Euler factor, f of level divisible by p) with Bellaiche (4)-(5) (two Euler factors, newform of level prime to p plus a chosen refinement) is exactly the second-Euler-factor point the stage names, and the Gauss-sum/2-pi-i dictionary between the two printed normalizations is recorded as an AUTHORED computation still to be verified. Three further hypotheses are carried explicitly: the modular-symbol comparison H^1_c = Hom_{Gamma_0}(Delta_0, -) needs the order of every torsion element of Gamma_0 to act invertibly; the control theorem needs slope STRICTLY less than k+1; and at critical slope a (k+1)-admissible distribution is NOT determined by its interpolation values, with Pollack-Stevens stating that their method does not give the missing values at x^{k+1}chi and Bellaiche proving that at a theta-critical point ALL the interpolation values vanish except in one Eisenstein case. All five stages are partial; no canonical integral period and no integrality statement for the measure was found in any source read.

nodes.title: Delta_0-valued modular symbols and the comparison with H^1_c, with the torsion hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, N prime to p, Gamma_0 = Gamma_1(N) intersect Gamma_0(p), and S_0(p) the semigroup of integral matrices (a b; c d) with p not dividing a, p dividing c and ad - bc nonzero. For a right Z[S_0(p)]-module M let M-tilde be the associated locally constant sheaf on the open modular curve Y_{Gamma_0}, and H^1_c(Gamma_0, M) = H^1_c(Y_{Gamma_0}, M-tilde). Set Delta_0 = Div^0(P^1(Q)) with its left GL_2(Q)-action by linear fractional transformations, and let S_0(p) act on the right on Hom(Delta_0, M) by (phi | gamma)(D) = phi(gamma D) | gamma. THEN, PROVIDED THE ORDER OF EVERY TORSION ELEMENT OF Gamma_0 ACTS INVERTIBLY ON M, there is a canonical Hecke-equivariant isomorphism H^1_c(Gamma_0, M) = Hom_{Gamma_0}(Delta_0, M). The U_p operator is realized explicitly by phi | U_p = sum over a = 0 to p-1 of phi | (1 a; 0 p).
hypotheses: The comparison is CONDITIONAL on the order of each torsion element of Gamma_0 acting invertibly on M. Pollack-Stevens list the sufficient conditions: N at least 4, or M a vector space over a field of characteristic 0, or Gamma_0 torsion-free, or M a Z_p-module with p > 3. This is exactly the elliptic-stabilizer point the stage insists on
M must be a right Z[S_0(p)]-module, not merely a Gamma_0-module; the U_p formula uses matrices of determinant p that lie in S_0(p) but not in Gamma_0
The Hecke algebra H is the free polynomial algebra over Z on T_l for l not dividing Np and U_q for q dividing Np
The involution comes from iota = (-1 0; 0 1), which normalizes Gamma_0; the decomposition into plus and minus eigenspaces requires 2 to act invertibly on M
Determinant twists: M(r) is M with the S_0(p)-action twisted by the r-th power of the determinant, and H^1_c(M(r)) = H^1_c(M)(r) where T_l acts by l^r T_l and U_q by q^r U_q
proofSteps: Form the local system M-tilde on Y_{Gamma_0} and its compactly supported cohomology.
Under the torsion hypothesis, quote the canonical isomorphism with Gamma_0-equivariant homomorphisms on degree-zero divisors ([2, Prop. 4.2] in Pollack-Stevens's numbering, i.e. Ash-Stevens).
Check Hecke equivariance and record the explicit U_p formula.
Record the determinant twist and the involution with their separate hypotheses.
acceptance: Check the comparison fails, or requires descent, for N < 4 with p = 2 or 3 and M integral
Verify the U_p formula against the q-expansion action on a weight-two symbol
Check H^1_c(M(r)) = H^1_c(M)(r) on a concrete twist

nodes.title: The interpolation formula for the analytic p-adic L-function, in two printed normalizations
nodes.statement: Let f be a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2. Two printed normalizations of the same interpolation property are recorded. (RJW, level Gamma_0(N) with p dividing N, alpha_p the U_p eigenvalue, v_p(alpha_p) < k+1): for every Dirichlet character chi of conductor p^n and every 0 <= j <= k, the integral of chi(x)x^j against L_p^an(f) equals -alpha_p^{-n} (1 - chi(p)p^j/alpha_p) G(chi) j! p^{nj} (2 pi i)^{-(j+1)} L(f,chi,j+1)/Omega_f^{pm}. (Pollack-Stevens, level Gamma_0 = Gamma_1(N) cap Gamma_0(p), slope h < k+1): mu_f(x^j chi) = a_p^{-n} p^{n(j+1)} (-2 pi i)^{-j} j! tau(chi^{-1})^{-1} L(f, chi^{-1}, 1)/Omega_f^{pm}. The two are NOT literally equal: they differ in the twist (chi versus chi^{-1}), in whether the Gauss sum appears in the numerator or the denominator, in the power of 2 pi i, and in the presence of the Euler factor. The printed last argument '1' of the Pollack-Stevens L-value is inconsistent with the j-dependence of both sides; Bellaiche, restating the same Pollack-Stevens interpolation property, prints L_infinity(f phi^{-1}, j+1), which is the reading under which the formula is consistent.
hypotheses: RJW: f has level Gamma_0(N) with p DIVIDING N, so L(f,s) is the L-function of the p-level form and carries only one Euler factor at p
RJW: the hypothesis is v_p(alpha_p) < k+1; the theorem does NOT cover v_p(alpha_p) = k+1, and RJW say so explicitly

Pollack-Stevens: chi is a finite order character of Z_p^x of conductor p^n; for n >= 1 one has chi(p) = 0 so the Euler factor in RJW's version is 1, and the two formulas can only be compared at n = 0 through the Euler factor

Both period normalizations Omega_f^{pm} are defined only up to a scalar: the plus/minus eigensymbols are normalized by a CHOICE (Pollack-Stevens normalize phi^{pm}_f to have size 1; Bellaiche says the formula holds 'up to a scalar independent on phi t^j')
The parity condition selecting the sign is phi(-1) = pm 1 (Bellaiche); it is not an extra hypothesis but part of the statement
proofSteps: Record RJW Theorem B.1 verbatim, with its growth clause (order v_p(alpha_p)) and its uniqueness clause.
Record Pollack-Stevens formula (2) verbatim from the page image.
Record Bellaiche formula (4) with its modification factor (5), which is the same interpolation property for a newform of level Gamma_1(N) with p prime to N and a chosen refinement.

AUTHORED RECONCILIATION (not quoted from any source): for chi primitive of conductor p^n one has G(chi) tau(chi^{-1}) = chi(-1) p^n, so p^{n(j+1)}/tau(chi^{-1}) = chi(-1) G(chi) p^{nj}; the residual discrepancies are a factor 2 pi i between (2 pi i)^{j+1} and (-2 pi i)^j and the sign chi(-1), both of which are absorbed into the choice of Omega_f^{pm}. This is the 'dictionary' the stage asks to prove; it is recorded here as a computation to be verified, not as a source statement.
acceptance: Check the n = 0 case of RJW Theorem B.1 separately: there G(chi) = 1, alpha_p^{-n} = 1 and the Euler factor 1 - p^j/alpha_p is the only surviving modification
Check that for n >= 1 the Euler factor is 1 because chi(p) = 0, so the two printed formulas differ only by the Gauss-sum and (2 pi i) conventions
Verify the Gauss-sum identity G(chi) tau(chi^{-1}) = chi(-1) p^n for chi primitive of conductor p^n and confirm the reconciliation above
Verify that the printed Pollack-Stevens L-argument must be j+1 by checking both sides at two different values of j

sources.locator: Appendix B.2.1, Theorem B.1, printed pp. 79-80
sources.excerpt: Let alpha_p denote the U_p eigenvalue of f. If v_p(alpha_p) < k+1, then there exists a unique locally analytic distribution L_p^an(f) in D^la(Z_p^x) on Z_p^x such that - L_p^an(f) has growth of order v_p(alpha_p). - For all Dirichlet characters chi of conductor p^n, and for all 0 <= j <= k, we have ... = -alpha_p^{-n} (1 - chi(p) p^j/alpha_p) G(chi) j! p^{nj}/(2 pi i)^{j+1} L(f,chi,j+1)/Omega_f^{pm}.
sources.match: The roadmap's normative statement, with the strict slope inequality and the uniqueness-from-growth clause.

sources.match: The second printed normalization. Its last L-argument is printed as 1, which cannot be right since the left side depends on j; the discrepancy is exactly the printed normalization problem the stage anticipates.

sources.excerpt: L^{pm}(f_beta, phi t^j) = e_p(beta, phi t^j) m^{j+1}/(-2 pi i)^j . j!/tau(chi^{-1}) . L_infinity(f phi^{-1}, j+1)/Omega_f^{pm} ... up to a scalar independent on phi t^j

nodes.title: The two refinements of a newform and the modification factor with both Euler factors
nodes.statement:
Let f be a newform of weight k+2 and level Gamma_1(N) with p prime to N, T_p f = a_p f and

f = epsilon(p) f. Let alpha, beta be the roots of X^2 - a_p X + epsilon(p) p^{k+1} (assumed distinct). The two refinements are f_alpha(z) = f(z) - beta f(pz) and f_beta(z) = f(z) - alpha f(pz); they are the two normalized forms of level Gamma = Gamma_1(N) cap Gamma_0(p) with the same T_l and diamond eigenvalues as f, and they satisfy U_p f_beta = beta f_beta and U_p f_alpha = alpha f_alpha. A REFINEMENT IS THE CHOICE OF A ROOT, not a property of f. For a refinement the interpolation factor is e_p(beta, phi t^j) = beta^{-nu} (1 - phi-bar(p) epsilon(p) p^{k-j}/D)(1 - phi(p) p^j/D), where nu is the p-part of the conductor of phi and D is the U_p eigenvalue of the chosen refinement; TWO Euler factors appear, because the L-function on the right is that of the level-prime-to-p NEWFORM f, not of the refinement.
hypotheses: p prime to N; alpha not equal to beta is assumed 'without loss of generality and for simplicity' by Bellaiche
Bellaiche also assumes throughout that p is ODD
When phi is ramified at p (nu >= 1) both Euler factors are 1 because phi(p) = phi-bar(p) = 0, and e_p reduces to beta^{-nu}; the Euler factors are visible only for phi unramified at p

PRINTED DISCREPANCY: Bellaiche's formula (5) prints alpha in BOTH Euler-factor denominators while the prefactor is 1/beta^nu and the L-function attached is that of the refinement f_beta with U_p f_beta = beta f_beta. Since alpha and beta are defined as the two distinct roots and beta is the eigenvalue of the refinement in question, the denominators should be beta. This is recorded as a printed inconsistency in the source, verified against Bellaiche's own Sec. 1.3 definitions
RJW Theorem B.1 has only ONE Euler factor because there f already has level divisible by p; converting to the good-prime newform is what produces the second factor
proofSteps: Form the two p-stabilizations by the displayed formulas and check the U_p eigenvalues from the q-expansions.
Record that the refinement is the choice of root, matching Bellaiche's 'The choice of a root beta or alpha of (1) is also called a refinement of f'.
Record the modification factor (5) with both Euler factors and flag the alpha/beta inconsistency in the printed denominators.
Compare with RJW Theorem B.1: the single factor (1 - chi(p)p^j/alpha_p) there is the second of Bellaiche's two factors specialized to the p-level form.
acceptance: Check U_p f_beta = beta f_beta directly from f_beta(z) = f(z) - alpha f(pz)
Check that for phi ramified the modification factor is beta^{-nu}
Check the alpha/beta discrepancy by specializing to an ordinary f and the ordinary refinement, where beta is a unit and alpha is not
Check the relation L(f_beta, s) = (1 - alpha p^{-s}) L(f, s) and confirm it produces exactly the missing Euler factor at unramified phi

sources.locator: Sec. 1.3, printed p. 4
sources.excerpt: As is well known, there are two normalized modular forms for Gamma = Gamma_1(N) cap Gamma_0(p) ... f_alpha(z) = f(z) - beta f(pz), f_beta(z) = f(z) - alpha f(pz). Those forms satisfy U_p f_beta = beta f_beta and U_p f_alpha = alpha f_alpha.
sources.match: The construction of the two refinements with the crossed roots, which is the source of the two Euler factors.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.3, printed p. 4
sources.excerpt: The choice of a root beta or alpha of (1) is also called a refinement of f. Refinements are also sometimes called p-stabilizations, but we shall not use this terminology.
sources.match: Confirms the stage's insistence that a refinement includes a chosen root and is not determined by f alone.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.4.2, formula (5), printed p. 8 (read from the 500 dpi page image)
sources.excerpt: e_p(beta, phi t^j) = (1/beta^nu)(1 - phi-bar(p) epsilon(p) p^{k-j}/alpha)(1 - phi(p) p^j/alpha)
sources.match: The modification factor as printed. The two Euler factors are the content; the alpha in their denominators is inconsistent with the 1/beta^nu prefactor and with Sec. 1.3's definitions, and is recorded here as a source typo rather than propagated.

nodes.title: The specialization map is an isomorphism on the slope < k+1 subspace
nodes.statement: Let D_k be the space of locally Q_p-analytic distributions on Z_p with the weight-k action of Gamma_0, and Sym^k(Q_p^2) its finite-dimensional quotient. The induced Hecke-equivariant specialization map H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k) -> H^1_c(Gamma_0, Sym^k(Q_p^2)) restricts to an ISOMORPHISM on the subspace where U_p acts with slope STRICTLY LESS THAN k+1. Consequently a slope-h eigensymbol phi_f with h < k+1 lifts uniquely to a Hecke-eigensymbol Phi_f, and integrating Phi_f over the divisor {infinity} - {0} and restricting to Z_p^x gives the p-adic L-function mu_f.
hypotheses: The strict inequality h < k+1 is essential; the theorem fails at slope exactly k+1, which is the whole point of the critical-slope work

The source of the isomorphism is the identification of the kernel of specialization with H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_{-2-k})(k+1), a twist by the (k+1)-st power of the determinant, on which U_p acts with slope at least k+1
The surjectivity on the slope-< k+1 part uses the Riesz decomposition for the compact operator U_p
Pollack-Stevens attribute the theorem to Stevens and cite [19] and [15, Thm. 5.12]; the proof is not reproduced in full in this paper
proofSteps: Identify the kernel of the specialization map with H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_{-2-k})(k+1); the determinant twist makes T_n act by n^{k+1}T_n, so U_p acts with slope at least k+1 there.
Riesz-decompose with respect to the compact operator U_p; on the slope-< k+1 part the kernel vanishes and specialization is surjective.
Deduce that specialization is an isomorphism on the slope-< k+1 part.
Define mu_f = Phi_f({infinity} - {0}) restricted to Z_p^x and quote Proposition 9.1 identifying it with the classical p-adic L-function.
acceptance: Check the twist computation: the kernel of D_k -> Sym^k is D_{-2-k}(k+1) and U_p there has slope at least k+1
Check the ordinary case h = 0 and recover a measure
Check the failure at h = k+1 by exhibiting a nonzero element of the kernel with the same eigenpacket

sources.locator: Sec. 1, Theorem 1.1, printed p. 2
sources.excerpt: H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k)^{(<k+1)} -> H^1_c(Gamma_0, Sym^k(Q_p^2))^{(<k+1)}. That is, the specialization map is an isomorphism on the subspace where U_p acts with slope strictly less than k+1.
sources.match: The control theorem the stage names, with the strict inequality visible.

sources.locator: Sec. 1, printed pp. 2-3
sources.excerpt: the kernel of the specialization map can be identified with H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_{-2-k})(k+1); here, we are twisting by the (k+1)st power of the determinant, and thus the Hecke operator T_n acts by n^{k+1} T_n. In particular, U_p acts with slope at
sources.match: The mechanism behind the slope bound; this is the intermediate machinery the stage asks to expose rather than package.

sources.locator: Sec. 9, Proposition 9.1, printed p. 22
sources.excerpt: With f, phi_f and Phi_f as above, we have Phi_f({infinity} - {0}) restricted to Z_p^x = mu_f, the p-adic L-function of f.
sources.match: The evaluation on the divisor {infinity} - {0} and restriction to units that the stage requires, identified with the classical p-adic L-function.

nodes.title: Pollack-Stevens: specialization is an isomorphism on the f-generalized eigenspace iff f is not in the image of theta^{k+1}
nodes.statement: Let f be an eigenform in S_{k+2}(Gamma_0, Q-bar_p) of slope exactly k+1, and let theta^{k+1} : M^dagger_{-k}(Gamma, Q_p) -> M^dagger_{k+2}(Gamma, Q_p) be the p-adic theta operator acting on q-expansions by (q d/dq)^{k+1}. Then H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(Gamma_0, P_k^dual)_{(f)} is an isomorphism IF AND ONLY IF f is not in the image of theta^{k+1}, where the subscript (f) is the GENERALIZED eigenspace. When f is not in that image, the unique eigensymbol Phi_f lifting phi_f defines mu_f = Phi_f({infinity} - {0}) restricted to Z_p^x, which is (k+1)-admissible and satisfies the interpolation property; when f IS in the image, there is a nonzero eigensymbol in the kernel of specialization.
hypotheses: The slope must be exactly k+1; the theorem is about the critical-slope subspace
The subscript (f) denotes the GENERALIZED eigenspace, not the eigenspace

A (k+1)-admissible distribution is NOT determined by the interpolation property alone: Pollack-Stevens state that one would also need the values at characters x^{k+1}chi, and that their method does not give those values

A WEAKER version (Theorem 6.7) is proved first under the stronger hypothesis that f has no mod p companion form; Proposition 6.9 shows f in the image of theta^{k+1} implies f has a mod p companion form

The proof of Theorem 8.1 uses the exact sequence 0 -> H^1_c(D_{-2-k})(k+1)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(D_k)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(P_k^dual)_{(f)} -> 0 together with Theorem 7.1 producing an overconvergent eigenform from an eigensymbol
proofSteps: Form the exact sequence of generalized eigenspaces with kernel H^1_c(D_{-2-k})(k+1)_{(f)}.

If a nonzero H-eigensymbol Psi exists in the kernel, untwist it and apply Theorem 7.1 to get an overconvergent eigenform g in M^dagger_{-k} with the same eigenpacket; then theta^{k+1} g has the eigenpacket of f, and comparing q-expansions gives f = theta^{k+1} g.
Conversely, if f = theta^{k+1} g, Theorem 7.1 produces an eigensymbol Psi_0 for g; twisting gives a nonzero element of the kernel.

Define mu_f from the unique lift in the non-theta-critical case; admissibility is quoted from [15, Lemma 6.2] and the interpolation property is formal from Phi_f being a U_p-eigensymbol lifting phi_f.
acceptance: Check that a (k+1)-admissible distribution is not determined by its values at x^j chi for 0 <= j <= k
Check Proposition 6.9: f in the image of theta^{k+1} implies f has a mod p companion form
Check Remark 8.2: when f is in the image of theta^{k+1} one cannot conclude from Theorem 7.1 alone that the kernel eigensymbol is unique up to scaling

sources.locator: Sec. 8, Theorem 8.1, printed p. 21 (read from the page image)
sources.excerpt: Let f be an eigenform in S_{k+2}(Gamma_0, Q-bar_p) with slope k+1. Then H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(Gamma_0, P_k^dual)_{(f)} is an isomorphism if and only if f is not in im(theta^{k+1}).
sources.match: The theorem, with the generalized-eigenspace subscript and the exact coefficient field Q-bar_p (the text layer of the PDF drops the bar; the statement was read from the rendered page).

sources.locator: Sec. 9, Remark 9.4, printed p. 22
sources.excerpt: Since mu_f is a (k+1)-admissible distribution, it is not uniquely determined by the above interpolation property. To uniquely determine this distribution by interpolation, one would also need to specify its values at the characters of the form x^{k+1} chi with chi of finite order. We point out here that our method of producing mu_f from overconvergent modular symbols does not directly give a way of understanding its values at such characters.
sources.match: Exactly the stage's requirement to 'prove the correct replacement for uniqueness'; the source states that uniqueness by interpolation FAILS and that its method does not supply the missing values.

sources.locator: Sec. 8, Remark 8.2, printed p. 21 (read from the page image)
sources.excerpt: When f is in the image of theta^{k+1}, the above theorem implies that there is an H-eigensymbol Psi in H^1_c(D_k)^{pm}_{(f)} which is in the kernel of specialization. However, from Theorem 7.1 alone, one cannot conclude that this symbol (up to scaling) is unique.
sources.match: The precise limitation in the theta-critical case, which Bellaiche later removes.

nodes.title: Bellaiche's one-dimensionality theorem for decent refinements and the vanishing of the interpolation values in the theta-critical case
nodes.statement: Let f be a newform of weight k+2 and level Gamma_1(N) (p odd, prime to N) and f_beta a refinement of f at p. Call f_beta DECENT if (i) f is Eisenstein, or (ii) f_beta is non-critical, or (iii) f is cuspidal and H^1_g(G_Q, rho_f) = 0. Assume f_beta is decent, and if f is Eisenstein that v_p(beta) > 0. Then for both signs the eigenspace Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)[f_beta] is ONE-DIMENSIONAL, and the following are equivalent: (i) f_beta is critical; (ii) the generalized eigenspaces Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)_{(f_beta)} have dimension strictly greater than 1; (iii) the specialization rho_k^*(Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)[f_beta]) = 0 for both signs. The L-functions are L^{pm}(f_beta, sigma) = Phi^{pm}_{f_beta}({infinity} - {0})(sigma), each defined only up to a nonzero scalar. THEOREM 2: if f_beta is theta-critical then L^{pm}(f_beta, phi t^j) = 0 for ALL finite-order phi and all 0 <= j <= k, with one exception (f Eisenstein, f_beta not critical, sign epsilon(f_beta), chi trivial and j = k). When f_beta is critical, dim Symb^{pm}(D_k)_{(f_beta)} = e > 1 equals the ramification degree of the weight map at the corresponding point of the eigencurve, which is smooth, and e-1 SECONDARY L-functions are defined by L^{pm}_i(f_beta, sigma) = (d^i L^{pm}(y,sigma)/dy^i) at y = x.
hypotheses: p ODD and prime to N throughout Bellaiche's paper
The 'decent' hypothesis is required; Bellaiche notes all CM forms are decent and that it is conjectured that every cuspidal form satisfies (iii)
For f Eisenstein one must additionally assume v_p(beta) > 0

The L-functions are defined only up to a nonzero scalar, since the generators Phi^{pm}_{f_beta} are; the secondary L-functions are only defined up to a scalar AND up to adding a linear combination of the earlier ones, so it is the FLAG F_0 contained in F_1 contained in ... that is well defined

Theorem 2's vanishing means the standard interpolation values do not determine the theta-critical L-function; the interpolation property (4) is recovered only by the TOP secondary L-function L^{pm}_{e-1}, while L^{pm}_i for 0 <= i <= e-2 satisfy the vanishing property (6)
The eigencurve is NOT etale over the weight space at a critical point, which Bellaiche identifies as the new difficulty in constructing the two-variable L-function
proofSteps: Construct the eigencurve inside the module of distribution-valued modular symbols over an affinoid of weight space, using the Riesz decomposition for U_p-slope <= nu, and compare with Coleman's construction via a theorem of Chenevier.
Use smoothness of the eigencurve at decent classical points plus a commutative-algebra argument to compute the eigenspace and generalized eigenspace dimensions (Theorem 1).
Define L^{pm}(f_beta,sigma) as the Mellin transform of Phi^{pm}_{f_beta}({infinity} - {0}).
Theorem 2's vanishing follows from (iii) of Theorem 1: theta-criticality forces the specialization of the eigensymbol to vanish, hence all the special values vanish.
Differentiate the two-variable L-function along the smooth curve to define the secondary L-functions and their interpolation properties.
acceptance: Check the exceptional case in Theorem 2 (f Eisenstein, f_beta not critical, chi trivial, j = k)
Check that for a critical-slope CM cuspform the ordinary interpolation values all vanish while the distribution does not
Check that e equals the ramification degree of the weight map at x
Check the divisibility reformulation: for theta-critical f_beta, s -> L^{pm}(f_beta, psi chi_s) is divisible by log^{[k]}(s) = product over i = 0 to k of log_p(gamma^{-j}s)

sources.locator: Sec. 1.4.1, Definition 1 and Theorem 1, printed pp. 5-6
sources.excerpt: Definition 1. We shall say that a refined form f_beta is decent if it satisfies at least one of the three following assumption: (i) f is Eisenstein (ii) f_beta is non-critical. (iii) f is cuspidal and H^1_g(G_Q, rho_f) = 0.
sources.match: The exact technical hypothesis under which Bellaiche's construction works; the stage requires the eigencurve/local-algebra conditions to be included rather than suppressed.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.4.1, Theorem 1, printed p. 6
sources.excerpt: Then for both choices of the sign pm, the eigenspace Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)[f_beta] has dimension 1. Moreover the following are equivalent (i) f_beta is critical. (ii) The generalized eigenspaces Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)_{(f_beta)} ... have dimensions strictly greater than 1. (iii) One has rho_k^*(Symb^{pm}_Gamma(D_k)[f_beta]) = 0.
sources.match: The one-dimensionality that replaces Pollack-Stevens' uniqueness, together with the criterion for criticality.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.4.3, Theorem 2 and formula (6), printed p. 8 (read from the page image)
sources.excerpt: If f_beta is theta-critical, then L^{pm}(f_beta, phi t^j) = 0 for all phi of finite order and 0 <= j <= k, excepted in the following case: f is Eisenstein, f_beta is not critical, the sign pm is epsilon(f_beta), the character chi is trivial, and j = k.
sources.match: The exact statement that at a theta-critical point the ordinary interpolation values all vanish while the distribution does not; this is the stage's warning made precise, with its single exception.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.4.5, printed pp. 10-11
sources.excerpt: Of course, the function L^{pm}_i(f_beta,sigma) is only defined up to a scalar and up to adding any linear combination of the L^{pm}_j(f_beta,sigma) for 0 <= j <= i-1. In other words, this is the flag F_0 contained in F_1 contained in ... contained in F_{e-1} in the space of analytic functions of sigma that is well defined
sources.match: The precise sense in which the secondary L-functions exist; a consumer must not treat them as individually well-defined functions.

nodes.title: The analytic, arithmetic and algebraic p-adic L-functions of a modular form and the relations among them
nodes.statement: For f a modular form: the ANALYTIC p-adic L-function is L_p^an(f) of Theorem B.1; the ARITHMETIC one is Log_{V_f}(z_Kato(f)) where z_Kato(f) is Kato's Euler system localized at p, living in H^1_Iw(Q_p, V_f), and Log_{V_f} is Perrin-Riou's big logarithm; the ALGEBRAIC one is L_p^alg(f) = ch_{Lambda(Z_p^x)}(X_{p^infinity}(V_f)), defined when f is p-ordinary and using Kato's theorem that the Selmer module is Lambda-torsion. Kato's explicit reciprocity law gives L_p^an(f) = L_p^arith(f) in D^la(Z_p^x). The Iwasawa Main Conjecture for f, L_p^alg(f) = (L_p^an(f)) inside Lambda(Z_p^x), is a theorem of Kato and Skinner-Urban UNDER SOME MILD ADDITIONAL TECHNICAL HYPOTHESES.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction requires f to be p-ORDINARY (v_p(alpha_p) = 0), so that V_f is p-ordinary in the sense of RJW Definition 13.19 and the analytic object is a measure rather than a mere distribution
The Lambda-torsionness of the Selmer module is Kato's theorem, not a definition
RJW state the Main Conjecture for f only 'under some mild additional technical hypotheses' and do not list them

The case alpha_p = 0 (infinite slope) is NOT covered by Theorem B.1; RJW point to Delbourgo for elliptic curves with additive reduction and to Rodrigues Jacinto for partial constructions via Kato's Euler system and Perrin-Riou's big logarithms
The critical-slope case v_p(alpha_p) = k+1 is covered by Pollack-Stevens and Bellaiche but with a DIFFERENT statement, as recorded in the L3 nodes
proofSteps: Record RJW's three constructions and the two comparison theorems (B.3 and B.4) as stated.
Record the attributions: B.2 and B.3 to Kato's Asterisque 295 paper, B.4 to Kato and Skinner-Urban.
Record the boundaries: the omitted technical hypotheses in B.4 and the uncovered alpha_p = 0 and v_p(alpha_p) = k+1 cases.
acceptance: Instantiate at a p-ordinary weight-two form attached to an elliptic curve and compare with the classical Mazur-Swinnerton-Dyer construction
Check that the growth condition of Theorem B.1 places L_p^an(f) in Lambda(Z_p^x) exactly when v_p(alpha_p) = 0
Check the supersingular case a_p = 0 where both refinements have slope (k+1)/2 and neither is ordinary

sources.locator: Appendix B.2.1, printed p. 80
sources.excerpt: We see that L_p^an(f) is, in this generality, only a locally analytic distribution (in the sense of Sec. 3.7). We note, however, that if f is p-ordinary (i.e. if v_p(alpha_p) = 0) then the growth condition implies that L_p^an(f) lies in the subspace of p-adic measures on Z_p^x.
sources.match: The exact criterion separating measures from distributions, which is the L2/L4 boundedness point.

sources.locator: Appendix B.2.2, Theorems B.2 and B.3, printed p. 80
sources.excerpt: Theorem B.3. - There is an equality L_p^an(f) = L_p^arith(f) in D^la(Z_p^x).
sources.match: Kato's explicit reciprocity law as the comparison between the analytic and arithmetic constructions.

sources.locator: Appendix B.2.3, Theorem B.4, printed p. 80
sources.excerpt: Theorem B.4 (Iwasawa Main Conjecture for f). - Under some mild additional technical hypotheses, we have L_p^alg(f) = (L_p^an(f)) inside Lambda(Z_p^x).
sources.match: The statement with its hypotheses left unspecified in the source; a consumer must not treat it as unconditional.

sources.locator: Appendix B.2.1, printed p. 80
sources.excerpt: If alpha_p is not 0, then we know that v_p(alpha_p) <= k+1, but the above theorem does not handle the case v_p(alpha) = k+1. ... The case of alpha_p = 0 is known as the infinite slope case.
sources.match: Delimits exactly which slopes Theorem B.1 covers, which is the boundary between stages L2, L3 and L4.

links.reason: The control theorem is a statement about H^1_c(Gamma_0, D_k) and its specialization to H^1_c(Gamma_0, Sym^k). Both spaces are the modular-symbol spaces of the L0 node, and the U_p-slope decomposition that drives the proof uses the explicit U_p formula phi | U_p = sum phi | (1 a; 0 p) on Hom_{Gamma_0}(Delta_0, -), which is available only under L0's torsion hypothesis. Moreover the identification of the kernel as H^1_c(D_{-2-k})(k+1) uses L0's determinant-twist identity H^1_c(M(r)) = H^1_c(M)(r).

sources.locator: Sec. 2.1-2.2 (printed pp. 4-5) used in Sec. 1 (printed pp. 2-3)

links.reason: Pollack-Stevens' critical-slope theorem is obtained by repeating the small-slope analysis on the slope-exactly-(k+1) subspace: the same exact sequence 0 -> H^1_c(D_{-2-k})(k+1)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(D_k)_{(f)} -> H^1_c(P_k^dual)_{(f)} -> 0 is used, but now the kernel can be nonzero and the theta operator decides when. The construction of mu_f from the unique lift is likewise copied from the non-critical case via Proposition 9.1.

sources.locator: proof of Thm. 8.1 (printed p. 21) reusing the sequence of Sec. 1 (printed pp. 2-3), and Def. 9.2 (printed p. 22) reusing Prop. 9.1

links.reason: Bellaiche's Theorem 1 covers the theta-critical cases that Pollack-Stevens explicitly leave open: Pollack-Stevens' Remark 8.2 says that when f is in the image of theta^{k+1} one cannot conclude uniqueness of the kernel eigensymbol from their Theorem 7.1, and their footnote records that Bellaiche subsequently proved the eigenspace is one-dimensional. Bellaiche states the same in Sec. 1.4.1: 'This theorem was known by a work of Stevens-Pollack in the case of forms f_beta that are not theta-critical ... the new cases provided of this theorem are the theta-critical cases.'

sources.locator: Remark 8.2 and footnote 3, printed pp. 2 and 21
Sec. 1.4.1, printed p. 6

links.reason: PROPOSED WITH A CAVEAT. The GL(1) side of RJW Appendix B.1 is the Kubota-Leopoldt pseudo-measure, whose evaluation at a character is exactly the pseudo-measure evaluation constructed in PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 (RJW formula (3.11)). For GL(2) the object is a locally analytic DISTRIBUTION, not a pseudo-measure, except in the p-ordinary case where the growth condition makes it a measure; so the supply used here is the evaluation-at-characters formalism and the measure-versus-distribution distinction, not the pseudo-measure theory itself. The atlas already records ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions as depending on PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras; this records which part is actually consumed.

gaps.title: Stage-ordering tension: L1's stated scope needs L2's refinement data
gaps.detail: THIS IS A FINDING ABOUT THE ATLAS, NOT ABOUT A SOURCE. Stage L1's text requires that 'the distinction between the L-function of a p-stabilized form and that of the original newform must be separately checked; converting to the good-prime newform introduces the second familiar Euler factor.' That comparison is exactly what separates RJW Theorem B.1 (f of level Gamma_0(N) with p dividing N, ONE Euler factor) from Bellaiche (4)-(5) (f a newform of level prime to p with a CHOSEN refinement, TWO Euler factors). The refinement data - the two roots alpha, beta of X^2 - a_p X + epsilon(p)p^{k+1} and the two p-stabilizations - is assigned by the atlas to stage L2, and data/atlas.json records the edge L1 -> L2 (L2 requires L1). No L2 -> L1 edge is proposed here, because adding one would create a two-cycle. VERIFIED: both printed interpolation formulas and the definitions of the refinements (Bellaiche Sec. 1.3, printed p. 4). RESOLUTION NEEDED BY THE ATLAS OWNER: either narrow L1 to the fixed-level statement and move the newform comparison to L2, or split the refinement definitions out of L2 into a prerequisite of L1.

gaps.title: Printed inconsistency in Bellaiche formula (5): alpha in the Euler-factor denominators
gaps.detail: Bellaiche Sec. 1.3 (printed p. 4) defines alpha and beta as the two distinct roots of X^2 - a_p X + epsilon(p)p^{k+1}, with U_p f_beta = beta f_beta. Formula (5) on printed p. 8, read from a 500 dpi render of the page, is e_p(beta, phi t^j) = (1/beta^nu)(1 - phi-bar(p)epsilon(p)p^{k-j}/alpha)(1 - phi(p)p^j/alpha). The prefactor uses beta while both Euler-factor denominators use alpha. Since the L-function being interpolated is that of the refinement f_beta, the denominators should be beta. VERIFIED: the definitions in Sec. 1.3, the printed form of (4) and (5), and the fact that the two Euler factors vanish for phi ramified. NOT VERIFIED: whether a published erratum or the published version (Ann. Sci. ENS 2012) corrects this. Next source action: compare with the published version of Bellaiche's paper, or with Mazur-Tate-Teitelbaum Sec. I where the modification factor is standard; neither is in the supplied library.

gaps.title: Printed inconsistency in Pollack-Stevens formula (2): the L-argument
gaps.detail: Pollack-Stevens Sec. 9 formula (2), read from a 220 dpi render of printed p. 21, is mu_f(x^j chi) = (1/a_p^n)(p^{n(j+1)}/(-2 pi i)^j)(j!/tau(chi^{-1}))(L(f,chi^{-1},1)/Omega_f^{pm}). The last argument of the L-function is printed as 1, but the left-hand side depends on j and no other factor supplies the missing dependence. Bellaiche formula (4), restating the SAME Pollack-Stevens interpolation property, prints L_infinity(f phi^{-1}, j+1). VERIFIED: both printed formulas, from page images. CONCLUSION RECORDED: the Pollack-Stevens argument must be read as j+1. Next source action: check the published J. London Math. Soc. version of Pollack-Stevens.

gaps.title: No source read supplies canonical integral periods or the integrality of the measure
gaps.detail: Stage L1 requires saturated integral modular-symbol lattices and canonical integral period choices up to O^x; stage L2 requires that boundedness alone gives coefficients in O[[G]][1/p] and not necessarily O[[G]]. NEITHER statement appears in any of the four sources read: Pollack-Stevens normalize phi^{pm}_f 'to have size 1' (a choice), Bellaiche works 'up to a scalar', RJW write Omega_f^{pm} without constructing it, and Amice-Velu work at level one. VERIFIED: that all four sources leave the period a choice. NOT VERIFIED: any integral normalization. Next source action: Vatsal, Integral periods for modular forms; or Greenberg-Vatsal; or Mazur-Tate-Teitelbaum Sec. I. None is in the supplied library. Barrera Salazar-Williams, p-adic L-functions for GL2 (papers/KI_BSW_PadicGL2.pdf) IS in the library and was not read; it may contain the integral statement.

gaps.title: Eichler-Shimura and the modular-symbol comparison are quoted, not proved
gaps.detail: Pollack-Stevens Sec. 2.1 cites '[2, Proposition 4.2]' (Ash-Stevens) for the isomorphism H^1_c(Gamma_0,M) = Hom_{Gamma_0}(Delta_0,M), and Sec. 9 invokes 'Eichler-Shimura theory and multiplicity one' for the one-dimensionality of the f-isotypic part. Neither is proved there and neither reference is in the supplied library. VERIFIED: the statements and their hypotheses. Next source action: A. Ash and G. Stevens, Modular forms in characteristic l and special values of their L-functions, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986); and Shimura's Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions Ch. 8.

gaps.title: Amice-Velu's admissibility machinery was skimmed, not decomposed
gaps.detail: Amice-Velu Theoreme III (printed p. 125) gives existence and uniqueness of G_lambda under v_p(lambda) < w+1 for a level-one Hecke cusp form of weight w+2. The mechanism is in Sec. IV (printed pp. 127-129): interpolation polynomials S_n^h, Propositions IV.3 and IV.4, and a continuity estimate for euclidean division by the polynomial product of Q_n(X/g^k). Those pages were read only as page images and skimmed. VERIFIED: the statement of Theoreme III with its slope condition. NOT VERIFIED: the admissibility/uniqueness proof. Next source action: read Amice-Velu Sections II-IV in the library copy (papers/KI_AmiceVelu_HeckeDistributions.pdf); the OCR text layer is poor, so page images are needed. The nebentypus and general-level versions are not in that paper.
